newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX heating oil steepens losses ahead of APIs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX heating oil steepens losses ahead of APIs.

text.p: NYMEX heating oil steepened its losses Tuesday afternoon as dealers expected this evening's oil inventory report from the American Petroleum Institute (API) to show a build in distillate stocks.

"Slowly but surely heating oil lost ground as the consensus seems to expect a build in distillate stocks reflecting the fact that we didn't have cold weather last week," said Ed Kevelson, director of refined products for Paribas Futures Inc.
At 1500 EST, February heat was off 1.49 cents at 72.15 cents a gallon, making a session low in the afternoon of 72.00.
Distillate stocks, which are comprised of heating oil and diesel, were expected to grow by more than one million barrels.
"Crude still seems to be the strongest, keeping above $26.00 with the spreads holding up despite a string of refinery turnarounds," said Kevelson.
February crude was 17 cents lower at $26.20 a barrel.
February gasoline was off 0.47 cent at 72.05 cents a gallon, partly supported by several major refiners shutting down their gasoline making units for seasonal maintenance through most of January.
Though this meant less crude would be used by the refiners, crude's Feb/March backwardation remained steady at 70 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
